reference.description: A frame Handle, such as ``frame_7f3a9c2e``: the baseline, such as the training rows.

candidate.description: A frame Handle to compare against ``reference``, such as the test rows.

repeats.description: Balanced subsampling repeats, from 1 to 100. More repeats steady ``mean_repeat_z``. Null means 5. Constraints: at least 1; at most 100.

scheme.description: ``split`` fits once per repeat on a 70/30 carve; ``cross_validation`` fits five times per repeat and scores every drawn row, at five times the cost. Null means ``split``.

seed.description: Seed of the subsampling, the carve and the classifier. Null means a fixed default, so the same call gives the same result. Constraints: at least 0; at most 4294967295.

anyOf.description: Every ``c2st`` dial. Null keeps every default.

min_rows.description: The size floor: the smaller frame needs at least this many rows, or the call fails with ``c2st_sample_floor``. Below 30 the test flags identical frames as different more often than it should. Null means 30. Constraints: at least 2.

min_samples_leaf.description: Fewest rows in a leaf of the classifier. Larger is smoother and harder to fool by memorising rows. Null means 5. Constraints: at least 1.

thresholds.description: The size floor and the classifier's leaf size, each with its default and range. Null keeps every default.

output.description: The pooled result of one Classifier Two-Sample Test over two frames.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Something left out of a result: a capped list was cut, or a Literal Field withheld. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut, or the path of the Literal Field withheld, such as ``top_values[].value``.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds; 0 for a withheld Literal Field or cut cells.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist; for a withheld Literal Field, how many values at that path are null; for cut cells, how many were cut.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.
Position 4, `reason`: ``cap`` when a list was cut to its cap; ``literal_policy`` when the Operator's Literal Policy is ``deny``; ``truncated`` when long text cells were cut to their character cap.

candidate_rows.description: Rows of ``candidate``. Each repeat draws the smaller frame's row count from each.

columns.description: Columns tested: those of ``reference`` that neither frame declares excluded or soft-excluded.

skipped.description: Columns of ``reference`` left out because a frame declares them excluded or soft-excluded.

seed.description: The seed used: yours, or the fixed default when you passed null.

mean_repeat_z.description: The headline: the mean of ``repeat_z``. Near 0 means the classifier could not tell the frames apart; about 2 or more means it could, so the frames differ.

repeat_z.description: One ``z`` per repeat, in repeat order: ``(accuracy - 0.5) * 2 * sqrt(n_test)``.

repeat_z_spread.description: Standard deviation of ``repeat_z``; 0 for one repeat. Large next to ``mean_repeat_z`` means the mean rests on lucky draws: raise ``repeats``.

train_accuracy.description: Mean training accuracy over the repeats. Near 1 beside a ``test_accuracy`` near 0.5 means the classifier memorised rows, which hides a difference rather than inventing one.

test_accuracy.description: Mean held-out accuracy over the repeats; 0.5 is chance.

n_test.description: Held-out rows scored in each repeat, half from each frame.

degenerate.description: True when every repeat's classifier predicted one frame for every row, so ``z`` says nothing. Compare larger frames, or lower ``thresholds.min_samples_leaf``.

unseen_category.description: True when a categorical or boolean value is in ``candidate`` and never in ``reference``.
